title: Complex models of a supplied sequential telescope
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ commutative. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex] and mapping-telescope triangles [def-kun-truncations]. Given any small sequence $(E_m,t_m)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, there are K-flat complexes $P_m$ with flat terms, chain maps $p_m:P_m\to P_{m+1}$ and isomorphisms $QP_m\simeq E_m$ carrying $Qp_m$ to $t_m$. Put $T=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\bigoplus_mP_m\to\bigoplus_mP_m)$, where $s\iota_m=\iota_{m+1}p_m$. Then $T$ is K-flat. For any supplied telescope triangle with vertex $K$ and legs $e_m:E_m\to K$, there is an isomorphism $QT\simeq K$ respecting the legs and the telescope triangle. For every complex $L$ of $\mathcal O$-modules there is a chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Tel}_m\operatorname{Tot}(P_m\otimes_{\mathcal O}L)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_{\mathcal O}L)$, with the standard cochain signs, respecting every telescope leg. It is natural in chain maps of $L$ and in compatible chain maps of the chosen strict sequence models, and induces the corresponding natural isomorphism in the derived category, also for morphisms represented by roofs of quasi-isomorphisms. If $R\to\mathcal O$ is a map from a constant commutative ring sheaf and $L$ has a commuting action of a commutative $R$-algebra $B$, the same comparison is $B$-linear, with $B$ acting only on $L$; no flatness of $B/R$ is assumed.

source.place: Derived colimits: Tags 090Z, 0CRH and 0CRI; K-flat resolutions: Tag 06YS; tensor exactness: Tag 06YM. The simultaneous complex-model and tensor-naturality formulation is agent-stated from these constructions.

proof.text: Choose complexes $G_m$ representing $E_m$. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] choose quasi-isomorphisms $G_m\to I_m$ with $I_m$ K-injective. The equivalence of [lem-sf-kinjective-replacement-triangulated] represents each $t_m$ by a homotopy class between $I_m$ and $I_{m+1}$; choose a chain representative $f_m:I_m\to I_{m+1}$. Thus $QI_m\simeq E_m$ carries $Qf_m$ to $t_m$. A sequence is the free category on its successor arrows, so define its longer arrows by composition; no relations between different paths need to be lifted.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, Hom computation (3); injectives.tex Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck; existence for module sheaves in sites-cohomology.tex Section 07A5

proof.text: Construct $P_m$ and quasi-isomorphisms $a_m:P_m\to I_m$ inductively, maintaining K-flatness, flat terms and $Q(a_{m+1}p_m)=Q(f_ma_m)$. For $m=0$ take [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] applied to $I_0$. Given $P_m,a_m$, apply [lem-pur-kflat-map-factorization] to $f_ma_m:P_m\to I_{m+1}$. It supplies a flat-term K-flat $P_{m+1}$, a chain map $p_m:P_m\to P_{m+1}$ and a quasi-isomorphism $a_{m+1}:P_{m+1}\to I_{m+1}$ with $f_ma_m$ homotopic to $a_{m+1}p_m$. Homotopic maps have the same image under $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $v_m:QP_m\simeq E_m$ to the composite of $Qa_m$ and the chosen identification. Then $v_{m+1}Qp_m=t_mv_m$. Countable dependent choice in the fixed universe supplies the entire induction.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat, including its flat-terms clause

proof.text: Put $A=\bigoplus_mP_m$ and $u=1-s$, with $s\iota_m=\iota_{m+1}p_m$. By [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum], $A$ and $T=C(u)$ are K-flat. By [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim], $QA$ with its displayed inclusions is the coproduct of the $QP_m$, and the localized cone triangle is their telescope triangle. The $v_m$ induce a coproduct isomorphism $v:QA\simeq\bigoplus_mE_m$; checking on $Q\iota_m$ gives $vQ(s)=s_Ev$. Apply TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $(v,v)$ and the supplied telescope triangle for $K$. This gives $w:QT\to K$ commuting with the second and connecting maps. Both first maps are isomorphisms, hence [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $w$ an isomorphism. In particular $wQ(j_m)=e_mv_m$, where $j_m:P_m\to T$ is $\iota_m$ followed by the inclusion of the unshifted summand $A^n\subset T^n=A^n\oplus A^{n+1}$ of the cone (the second map of the cone triangle). No uniqueness of $w$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 090Z, definition-derived-colimit; Tag 0CRH, remark-uniqueness-derived-colimit; Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YR and 07A3 for K-flat closure

proof.text: Write $\otimes$ for the direct-sum total tensor. By [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], the canonical maps $\bigoplus_m(P_m\otimes L)\to A\otimes L$ are isomorphisms in every total degree: interchange the two coproduct indices and distribute sheaf tensor over coproducts. Here commutativity of $\mathcal O$ gives the same assertion in either tensor variable, by the sheafified flip $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$. On a generator $x\otimes l$, $x\in P_m^a,l\in L^b$, the differential is $d_Px\otimes l+(-1)^ax\otimes d_Ll$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], on both sides. Thus these maps form a chain isomorphism $\beta$. Checking on each $m$ gives $\beta s_{P\otimes L}=(s\otimes1)\beta$. Consequently $\beta$ induces the same isomorphism on both copies in the telescope endomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03EP, lemma-tensor-commute-colimits (2); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YM, lemma-derived-tor-exact, explicit total tensor construction

proof.text: Define $\Phi:\operatorname{Tel}_m(P_m\otimes L)\to T\otimes L$ by $\beta$ on the unshifted cone copy, and by the same coproduct rearrangement on the shifted copy: a generator $x\otimes l$ with $x\in P_m^a,l\in L^b$, in degree $a+b-1$, is sent to the summand $P_m^a\subset A^a\subset T^{a-1}$ tensored with $L^b$. No sign is inserted. On the unshifted copy the differentials agree by Step 4. On this shifted generator the left differential has terms $u(x)\otimes l$ in the unshifted copy, $-d_Px\otimes l$, and $-(-1)^ax\otimes d_Ll$. On the right the same three terms have coefficients $1,-1,(-1)^{a-1}$, respectively, so agree. The inverse is the reverse coproduct rearrangement on both copies. These generator formulas determine maps of sheaves since tensor and coproduct are obtained by sheafifying their presheaf constructions. Thus $\Phi$ is a chain isomorphism. The telescope leg lands in the unshifted copy, where the formula is precisely $j_m\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 06YM, lemma-derived-tor-exact; derived.tex definition-cone, cone differential and total tensor signs

proof.text: For a compatible chain map $r_m:P_m\to P'_m$ and $h:L\to L'$, all squares for $\Phi$ commute on the generators in both copies: both composites send $x\otimes l$ to $r_m(x)\otimes h(l)$. This proves strict naturality, including identities, compositions and all legs. For derived descent, the coefficient functors $P_m\otimes-$ and $T\otimes-$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], since $P_m$ and $T$ are K-flat with flat terms: flatness of the terms of $T$ follows from [lem-pc-kflat-closure] and the cone formula $T^n=A^n\oplus A^{n+1}$. The telescope on the left also preserves such maps: in the strict naturality square three sides become isomorphisms after $Q$, hence so does the fourth. Therefore the naturality equality extends to any coefficient roof $L\leftarrow H\to L'$ by inverting its quasi-isomorphism in that equality.

source.place: Tag 06YP, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism; Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor; total cone formula; derived.tex Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category

proof.text: For an objectwise quasi-isomorphism $r$ of strict flat-term K-flat sequence models, $\bigoplus_mr_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Indeed, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] makes $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ Grothendieck: its countable sums are filtered colimits of finite biproducts, hence exact; [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] then gives $H^n(\bigoplus r_m)=\bigoplus H^n(r_m)$. The induced map $T\to T'$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] applied to the localized cone triangles. Its cone is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] and K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum]. By [lem-pur-acyclic-kflat-tensor-arbitrary], tensoring that cone with any $L$ remains acyclic (that node places the K-flat factor on the right; the signed flip $x\otimes l\mapsto(-1)^{ab}l\otimes x$, a chain isomorphism since $\mathcal O$ is commutative, moves it to the left). The explicit two-copy formula of Step 5 applies to every cone map, and identifies this tensor with the cone of $T\otimes L\to T'\otimes L$. Thus the latter map is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of $\Phi$ proves the same for the left side. Invert these maps in the strict naturality equality to obtain naturality for roofs of compatible strict models as well. This is localization of the specified strict diagram maps, not a choice of functorial cones for arbitrary squares in $D(\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Tags 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side, and 06YM, lemma-derived-tor-exact; derived.tex Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic; derived.tex lemma-direct-sums; injectives.tex Tag 079P

proof.text: Suppose $R\to\mathcal O$ and a commuting $B$-action on $L$ are supplied. On a tensor generator define $b(x\otimes l)=x\otimes bl$, on either cone copy. This is well-defined because the actions of $B$ and $\mathcal O$ on $L$ commute and have the same $R$-action. Every differential commutes with $b$ since $L$ is a complex with that action, and every component of $\Phi$ commutes with $b$ by its generator formula. The same holds for the inverse, the legs and naturality squares for action-preserving maps. Hence the comparison and its derived localization are $B$-linear. No tensoring over $R$ with $B$, and no exactness assertion for $B\otimes_R-$, occurs, so flatness of $B/R$ is unnecessary.
